chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who owes a portion of [fasts] from the month of Ramadan, and then the next month of Ramadan catches him [before he makes them up]. He said: If he was sick in between, until the next month of Ramadan caught him, then there is not upon him except fasting, if he is healthy. But if the illness continues upon him, then upon him is to feed a poor person for each day.

key_terms.طَآئِفَة: A portion or part (of the missed fasts)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who misses fasting in Ramadan due to illness and does not make it up before the next Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Ishtibār clarifies the Shia juristic view that persistent illness excuses one from the penalty of fidya (feeding the poor) for delayed qada, distinguishing it from mere negligence. It establishes that if the illness extends through the subsequent Ramadan, the obligation shifts to feeding a poor person for each missed day, reflecting the principle that hardship alleviates financial burdens. This ruling underscores the mercy in Shia fiqh, where the cause of delay (illness) determines the specific expiation required.
